questions.q: What actually makes a function "dynamic" in modern Excel?
options: It returns multiple values that spill automatically into neighboring cells, resizing itself as the source data changes
It updates its font color automatically
It can only be used inside a PivotTable
It requires Ctrl+Shift+Enter to work
questions.explain: A dynamic array function spills its full result into neighboring cells the moment you press Enter, and reshapes that spill automatically if the source data changes size.

questions.q: How did a legacy array formula have to be entered, and what was its key limitation?
options: With Ctrl+Shift+Enter, and it always returned a fixed-size result that didn't grow with the source data
With a single click on the Formulas tab, and it had no limitations
With Alt+Enter, and it could only return one value
By typing curly braces manually around the formula
questions.explain: Legacy CSE (Ctrl+Shift+Enter) array formulas locked in a fixed result size at entry time — growing the source range meant re-entering the whole formula.

questions.q: What is the visual signal that a range of cells is a single spilled dynamic array formula, not several independent formulas?
options: A thin blue border Excel draws automatically around the spill range when a cell inside it is selected
A red squiggly underline
The cells turn bold automatically
A pop-up dialog box appears
questions.explain: Excel outlines a spilled range with a light blue border whenever any cell inside it is selected, confirming it's one live formula's output.

questions.q: If you click a cell in the middle of a spilled array (not the top-left cell), what happens in the formula bar?
options: It shows the same formula, dimmed and not directly editable, since only the top-left cell actually holds it
It shows a blank formula bar
It shows a #SPILL! error
It lets you fully edit and overwrite that one cell's formula independently
questions.explain: Only the top-left cell of a spill range holds the actual formula — every other cell in the range shows it dimmed/ghosted and read-only.

questions.q: Which of these is NOT one of the dynamic array functions covered in this chapter?
options: VLOOKUP
FILTER
SORT
UNIQUE
questions.explain: VLOOKUP is a legacy lookup function (Chapter 2) that returns a single value and isn't dynamic-array-aware; FILTER, SORT, and UNIQUE are this chapter's core dynamic array functions.
